questions.q: Butan-2-yltrimethylammonium hydroxide is heated. The major alkene is:
questions.explain: The bulky –N⁺(CH₃)₃ group makes hydroxide remove the most accessible β-hydrogen, on the CH₃ group, so the least substituted alkene is major (Hofmann rule). But-2-ene, the Saytzeff alkene, is the trap.

questions.q: What is the role of moist Ag₂O in the Hofmann elimination sequence?
options: It oxidises the amine to an amine oxide
It acts as a dehydrating agent
It exchanges iodide for hydroxide, precipitating AgI
questions.explain: Moist silver oxide converts the quaternary ammonium iodide into the hydroxide; this OH⁻ is the base that carries out the E2 elimination on heating. Amine oxides belong to the Cope elimination.

questions.q: The Hofmann (least substituted) alkene is the major product in the Hofmann elimination mainly because:
options: the least substituted alkene is the most stable
the reaction proceeds through a carbocation that rearranges
the large –N⁺(CH₃)₃ leaving group crowds the conformation needed for the more substituted alkene, so the most exposed β-H is removed
hydroxide is a very bulky base
questions.explain: The bulky, positively charged leaving group on the substrate controls the selectivity; the more substituted alkene is still the more stable one.

questions.q: N-Methylpyrrolidine is subjected to Hofmann exhaustive methylation (CH₃I, then Ag₂O and heat) until the nitrogen is removed completely. The final hydrocarbon and the number of cycles needed are:
questions.explain: The first cycle only opens the ring, giving CH₂=CH–CH₂–CH₂–N(CH₃)₂; a second cycle removes the nitrogen as trimethylamine and leaves buta-1,3-diene. A ring nitrogen has two C–N bonds to break, so two cycles are needed.
